item.title: On This Day: Champion horse Shergar kidnapped in Co Kildare
item.description: In February 1983, Shergar was kidnapped from his stable in Co Kildare, held for ransom, and brutally killed by his captors who haven't been identified.

item.title: On This Day: Brendan Behan, the Dublin playwright, rebel and raconteur, was born
item.description: Born on February 9, 1923, Behan became one of Ireland’s most notorious and celebrated writers - the author of "Borstal Boy" and plays such as "The Quare Fellow" and "The Hostage" - whose life of republican activism and hard-living fuelled his sharp satire.

item.title: When a calf was born with perfect heart-shaped patch on Valentine's Day in Antrim
item.description: James McAuley welcomed "Be My Valentine," a newborn Jersey calf with a heart patch on its forehead, to his farm in Bushmills, Co Antrim farm Valentine's Day in 2020.

item.title: St Valentine’s Day tips from our professional Irish matchmaker
item.description: Professional Irish matchmaker Maureen Tara Nelson gives helpful advice to those looking for love for Valentine's Day.

item.title: Rediscovering Mammy’s buns: The classic Irish sweet treat you’ll love to bake
item.description: "Fairy cakes, queen cakes, cupcakes or buns – these little classics were a staple growing up, especially at a party."

item.title: Martin Hayes to launch new annual St Patrick's Day series at Carnegie Hall
item.description: Irish Arts Center joins Carnegie Hall and Askonas Holt to present Martin Hayes and the Common Ground Ensemble on March 17, 2026 in a multi-year partnership celebrating Irish music.

item.title: Brad Pitt fever hits Ireland as filming locations are revealed
item.description: The actor is reportedly spending two weeks in Ireland shooting scenes for the upcoming A24 drama "One for All."

item.title: Revealed: Oscar winner Cillian Murphy’s ambitious vision for Dingle cinema
item.description: Oscar winner Cillian Murphy and his wife Yvonne McGuinness risked "shooting themselves in the foot" with their openness in regenerating the Phoenix Cinema in Dingle – but the risk is paying off, with locals "really embracing" the couple’s ambitious vision.

item.title: Lost Irish Famine item returns to Skibbereen from Canada after 165 years
item.description: Donor from Ontario brings 1859 silver samovar honoring Famine hero Dr. Dan Donovan back to Skibbereen Heritage Centre, in Cork.

item.title: Trump loses support of Irish as AOH releases statement
item.description: Ancient Order of Hibernians condemns a racist depiction of Barack and Michelle Obama shared from President Trump’s social media account and calls for accountability.
